raw.rationale: This candidate retains the rank-1 geometry that produced a strong low resonance at 2.45 GHz and only reduces the middle slot length l2 from 15.00 to 14.00 mm. By keeping the other rank-1 dimensions unchanged, the proposal aims to pull the high resonance toward 4.50 GHz while maintaining the low-band match, thereby improving the interpolated 4.50 GHz S11 margin.

raw.rationale: The two highest-ranked evaluated geometries share the same substrate and slot dimensions except l2=15.00 mm and l2=14.90 mm, and both produce two resonances near 2.45 GHz and 4.52-4.53 GHz with fixed-target S11 below -15 dB. Choosing l2=14.95 mm interpolates between those measured designs while keeping all other dimensions identical, which preserves the strong low-band match and should keep the high resonance close enough to 4.50 GHz to avoid the weaker 4.50 GHz target response seen when l2 drops to 14.83 mm.

raw.rationale: The rank-3 sample with l2=14.90 mm retained the same otherwise strong geometry used by the top-ranked designs, and it produced resonances at 2.44 GHz and 4.52 GHz with target S11 values of -25.70 dB and -15.55 dB. Compared with rank-1 at l2=15.00 mm, the slightly reduced middle slot length moved the high resonance closer to the 4.50 GHz target and improved the fixed-frequency high-band match while keeping the low resonance near 2.45 GHz. This complete design is therefore proposed as a neighboring alternative that uses only the observed stable high-performing geometry and gives margin below the -15 dB threshold at both required frequencies.
